title: Batches and the branch they determine — fixture

objectives.title: Ship the product in unattended windows

runs.title: Seed work, before any batch
runs.summary: Completed before batches were declared; belongs to none.
runs.full_description: NO batch key: membership is optional, and this run proves a batch-less run is legal in a roadmap that declares batches.

runs.title: Alpha: risky piece of night A
runs.summary: Sits in NIGHT-A; its consumers in other batches wait for a person.
runs.full_description: In batch NIGHT-A. Work that needs human review before anything DOWNSTREAM of it is trusted — but no run of ITS OWN batch waits on that review, which is exactly the grouping rule.

runs.title: Beta: builds on alpha inside night A
runs.summary: Same batch as alpha, plain depends_on edge.
runs.full_description: In batch NIGHT-A with a PLAIN depends_on edge on alpha: inside one batch, waiting for work to EXIST is legal — only waiting for its human approval deadlocks.

runs.title: Gamma: second reviewed piece of night A
runs.summary: Second approval-needing run in the SAME batch, no internal approval edge.
runs.full_description: In batch NIGHT-A. Several runs needing human approval MAY share a batch — the approval happens once, over the whole batch, at its end. What none of them may do is wait on EACH OTHER’s approval.

runs.title: Delta: night B consumes reviewed alpha
runs.summary: Cross-batch human-approval edge: legal, and the point of the model.
runs.full_description: In batch NIGHT-B, waiting on the HUMAN APPROVAL of alpha (NIGHT-A). A cross-batch approval edge marks where an unattended window ends: night A must be approved before this run of night B is dispatched.

runs.title: Omega: unbatched consumer of gamma
runs.summary: A batch-less run may wait on the approval of a batched one.
runs.full_description: NO batch key, waiting on the human approval of gamma (NIGHT-A): the consumer sits outside every batch, so no shared-batch deadlock is possible.
